subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Sam / Carlos — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap from my side and suggested next steps so we have alignment before the technical POC. TL;DR: FintechCo is looking to remove reliance on proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI / Anthropic) to reduce cost and control data residency while keeping parity on function-calling, safety, and latency.

Pain points we heard
- High per-token spend with current OpenAI usage for both chat and embedding workloads.
- Vendor lock concerns and limited ability to run in VPC/on-prem for regulated data.
- Need for function-calling/tooling compatibility and audited safety/filters.
- Latency variability during peak trading hours (spikes > 800ms for short chat flows).

Current stack (as discussed)
- Prod: OpenAI Chat + embeddings (mostly GPT-4/4o for policy checks); Anthropic used in a few internal tools.
- Orchestration: Custom service layer that routes between providers; heavy reliance on provider-specific response shapes and function-calling semantics.
- Infra: Kubernetes on AWS, some data in a dedicated VPC for PII-sensitive workloads.

Success criteria for a migration proof-of-concept
1) Feature parity: function-calling / structured outputs must work for your integration without major engineering changes.
2) Latency: p99 for conversational flows should be under 500ms for the critical path.
3) Cost: target 40% unit cost reduction vs. current OpenAI spend for comparable throughput.
4) Security & compliance: ability to run in VPC or private deployment and provide KMS/HSM integration + audit logs.
5) Safety: comparable or improved content filtering and policy controls.

Model shortlist (initial recommendations)
- Llama 3 family (eval for chat + system prompts)
- Mistral / Mistral-instruct variants (good baseline for cost/perf)
- RedPajama / Open-instruct checkpoints for embedding/structured-output evaluation

Proposed next steps
- Technical POC: 2-week scoped test (we supply a POC config and baseline prompts; FintechCo supplies representative traffic and evaluation prompts).
- Security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence (I attached our migration-playbook.pdf and sample-pricing.pdf).
- Schedule: Suggested kickoff window next week; we can run the POC in your VPC/dedicated environment or on Redwood Dedicated depending on your preference.

Can you confirm: (a) the three success criteria above capture your priorities, and (b) whether you prefer the POC in your VPC or Redwood Dedicated?

Attachments: migration-playbook.pdf, sample-pricing.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call to finalize the POC scope.

Best,
Marissa Cole

- Metrics: in the POC, we want to run both regular traffic and a spike window to validate latency SLOs.
